label: sorede
title: それで
meaning: and then, after that; Due to that そして、その後；それだから、そういうわけで
meaning_example: Then, what happened? /Due to a early frost, the apple harvest will be small this year.

notes.text: それでis quite different from それでいて but relates well with それでも、それでこそ、それでは、and それでなくても.
notes.html: それでis quite different from それでいて but relates well with それでも、それでこそ、それでは、and それでなくても.

examples.japanese: 朝寝坊した、それで仕事に遅れたんだ。
examples.body_text:
朝寝坊した、それで仕事に遅れたんだ。 

		I overslept and, 
		due to that, 
		was late for work.
examples.body_html:
朝寝坊した、それで仕事に遅れたんだ。 
I overslept and, due to that, was late for work.

comments.text:
Tigertさん, I think that in ex #, my dear is some expression of irony. The general meaning seems to be that the old man was victim of a trap and is now promising another one to his adversary.

In ex# I suppose the japanese text ends in "か？" and not in "かい？".

(Thanks for your explanation here below. )

comments.text: 赤毛　I think the かい　used in [#] is right. か　and かい have the same function where か　is a general purpose form and [かい] is used to speak to indivduals that are lower than you on the social ladder.
